The graph of the continuous function $y=f(x)$ is shown above. The points $A,B,$ and $C$ lie on the curve and have $x$-coordinates $x=-3,$ $x=0,$ and $x=3.$ Given that ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ at $A,B,$ and $C,$ find the intervals where ${f}^{′}(x)>0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We have ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ at the critical points $A$ and $B.$ Note the following:

- If $f(x)$ is strictly increasing, then ${f}^{′}(x)>0.$

- If $f(x)$ is strictly decreasing, then ${f}^{′}(x)<0.$

The information about ${f}^{′}(x)$ can be summarized in the following table:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & (-\infty ,-3) & -3 & (-3,0) & 0 & (0,3) & 3 & (3,\infty ) \\ f & ↗ & \text{max} & ↘ & \text{no extr.} & ↘ & \text{min} & ↗ \\ {f}^{′} & + & 0 & - & 0 & - & 0 & +\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(x)>0$ on the intervals $(-\infty ,-3)$ and $(3,\infty ).$
